# Independent Page rows fixtures

Original authored test material, generated by `generate.py` with ReportLab 4.4.9, `invariant=1`, uncompressed streams and the standard Helvetica font. No application/PDF.js code is used to generate the PDFs. These fixtures may be distributed with the project.

Regenerate using a Python environment with ReportLab 4.4.9:

```
python3 test/fixtures/pdf-page-order/generate.py
```

- `row-major.pdf` and `column-major.pdf` have identical text and coordinates. Only drawing order differs. Page rows expects `Left top Right top\nLeft bottom Right bottom` for both.
- `changed-word.pdf` changes the bottom-right text to `Right changed`; the ordered text must retain that difference.
- `mixed-fonts.pdf` aligns 10-point and 18-point strings on the same baseline and has a separate lower line. Expected `Small Large\nNext line`.
- `sideways.pdf` has page rotation 90 and text that is sideways in the displayed viewport. Page rows must reject it explicitly.
- `rotated-horizontal.pdf` has page rotation 90 with matching content rotation so its displayed baseline is horizontal LTR. Expected `Rotated horizontal`.
- `overlap.pdf` draws two distinct words at the same location. Page rows must reject ambiguous overprinting rather than drop either item.

`test/pdf-page-order.test.cjs` obtains actual PDF.js text items and display viewports, passes them to the pure ordering module, and checks original bytes remain unchanged. Synthetic controls additionally cover cancellation, item/output limits, whitespace fragments, Unicode, baseline tolerance, permutations, unsupported direction, skew and malformed geometry. Fixtures qualify this narrow horizontal-LTR ordering policy, not arbitrary layout reconstruction or human column-reading inference.
